title: She Tried Every Key. Then She Changed the Door.

shots.caption: THE DOOR WAS ALWAYS LOCKED.
shots.beat: WIDE: night stone wall, GIANT wooden door about five times her height: brass lock plate + keyhole + lever handle on the RIGHT edge, three big rusty hinges on the LEFT edge. Tiny Mira (yellow wristband + yellow satchel) walks in jingling a big ring of keys, stops, looks up. Slow push-in.
CLOSE: Mira stands on tiptoe, pushes a key into the huge lock, twists with both hands; key bends with a clank; she shakes stung hand.

shots.caption: SHE TRIED EVERY KEY.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: rapid tries — key after key tossed onto a growing pile beside her; last throw makes her stumble back.
DETAIL/POV: keyhole close-up; a pale silver glimmer (moonlight from a window inside the room) flickers behind it. Mira's eye appears at the hole.

shots.caption: SO SHE MADE HER OWN.
shots.beat: HOME BENCH: tiny room, desk lamp. Mira files a key blank clamped in a vise; bright metal shavings curl and fall; she wipes her brow.
DETAIL: the finished golden key raised into lamp light; she blows dust off and smiles wide.
WIDE TRACKING: Mira strides across a night bridge holding the shining key forward. In the background a tall figure in a BLUE scarf (Oto) is on a ladder oiling a squeaky lamp post, oil can in hand.

shots.caption: IT STILL WOULD NOT TURN.
shots.beat: CLOSE: golden key in lock; she hangs her whole weight on it, feet lift off ground; nothing moves.

shots.caption: THEN THE HANDLE BROKE.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: she grips the door handle with both hands and leans back pulling; handle snaps off; she falls on her back clutching it.
CLOSE FACE: sitting on ground, staring at broken handle in her hands; brows tilt, mouth turns down, one tear drop.

shots.caption: MAYBE IT WAS NOT HER DOOR.
shots.beat: HIGH WIDE: tiny figure slumped against the giant door, keys scattered, moon above.

shots.caption: SHE COULD HAVE WALKED AWAY.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: she stands, drops the handle into her bag, walks away from the door; slows; stops mid-step.
MEDIUM: she turns back; head tilts; camera pans from her face to the LEFT edge of the door: the three rusty hinges she has never touched.

shots.caption: THEN SHE LOOKED AT THE HINGES.
shots.beat: DETAIL: huge rusty lower hinge; her small finger touches it; rust flakes fall; its pin is jammed and sticks out.
MEDIUM: she pushes the hinge side with her shoulder; door creaks a hair; dust trickles from above.

shots.caption: A STRANGER STOPPED.
shots.beat: WIDE: Oto (the blue-scarf man from the bridge, ~1.35x taller) walks in from the right carrying his ladder and oil can, hearing the creaks; stops beside her.
TWO-SHOT: Mira holds up the broken handle, then points up at the top hinge. Oto follows her finger, nods, and leans his ladder against the hinge side.

shots.caption: HE BROUGHT THE OIL.
shots.beat: LOW ANGLE: Oto on the ladder oils the top and middle hinges (drips fall), then pulls both of their pins out; Mira steadies the ladder.

shots.caption: SHE USED THE BROKEN HANDLE.
shots.beat: CLOSE: Mira hammers the last, lowest hinge pin upward with the broken handle; tap, tap, tap; the pin slides out; she grins.

shots.caption: THEY PULLED TOGETHER.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: with all hinge pins out, Mira and Oto grip the hinge edge and pull, legs braced; the door starts pivoting on its still-locked latch side.

shots.caption: THE DOOR OPENED THE OTHER WAY.
shots.beat: WIDE: the giant door swings open on the hinge side, pivoting around the lock; pale dawn light from a far window spills out; both lean back, shielding their eyes.

shots.caption: BUT THERE WAS NO PRIZE.
shots.beat: INSIDE: empty dusty room, cobwebs, a window with first dawn light, bare walls. Nothing glitters. Mira and Oto stand in the giant doorway.
CLOSE FACE: Mira's disappointed face, shoulders drop; Oto's hand rests on her shoulder.

shots.caption: ONLY A BOX OF OLD TOOLS.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: she walks to a corner, opens a dusty toolbox: hammer, saw, files glint.
CLOSE: she lifts the hammer, looks back at the broken door handle and the old key pile; eyebrows rise; idea spark above head.

shots.caption: SO THEY GOT TO WORK.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: Mira turns the stuck lock bolt open from the inside with the hammer and screws the broken handle onto the INSIDE of the door; Oto taps the oiled pins back into all three hinges; Oto hangs a lamp that lights the room. The door now swings normally on its hinges.

shots.caption: SHE KEPT THE DOOR OPEN.
shots.beat: WIDE: Mira wedges a block under the open door so it can never shut; dusts hands.
DOORWAY: a small kid stick figure (red cap) peeks around the door edge, shy.

shots.caption: AND MADE ROOM FOR SOMEONE ELSE.
shots.beat: MEDIUM: Mira waves the kid in, kneels and hands her a small file and a key blank.

shots.caption: OTHERS BEGAN TO BUILD.
shots.beat: WIDE EXTERIOR at dawn: more figures walk through the open door carrying planks and boxes; the kid carries the old pile of failed keys inside.

shots.caption: THE EMPTY ROOM BECAME A WORKSHOP.
shots.beat: WIDE INTERIOR: room alive — benches, lamps; five people working: Mira hammering, Oto sawing, the kid filing, two new makers carrying a plank and painting.
DETAIL: the pile of failed keys now hangs as a wind chime by the window, Mira's golden key in the middle, tinkling in the breeze.
CLOSE: Mira and Oto nod to each other; she hands him a newly made key; he laughs and hangs it on the chime.
MEDIUM: Mira sits with the kid at a bench teaching her to file a key; the kid holds up her finished key and it shines.

shots.caption: SOME DOORS OPEN ANOTHER WAY.
shots.beat: WIDE EXTERIOR: dawn sun, the giant door wide open, lamps and figures inside; slow pull-back reveals, far down the street, another locked giant door with rusty hinges.

shots.caption: WHICH DOOR ARE YOU STILL PUSHING?
shots.beat: END CARD: glowing open-door outline, Mira and the kid silhouetted in it; small 'LIKE & SUBSCRIBE' tag under the question; music resolves.

creative_intent.logline: Over one night a tiny stick-figure maker tries every key on a giant locked door, breaks its handle, then notices the rusty hinges; with a stranger's oil and her broken handle she opens the door the other way, finds only an empty room and old tools, and turns it into a workshop with an open door for others.
creative_intent.hook: 0-5s: a tiny stick figure with a jingling ring of keys walks up to a giant door about five times her height and looks up.
creative_intent.theme: When pushing harder on the same lock fails, look at the problem from another side, accept help, and keep the door open for others.
creative_intent.character_bible: Mira (lead): small, round head, thin dark-ink-outlined off-white stick body, signature YELLOW wristband on right wrist + small yellow tool satchel. Oto (helper): ~1.35x taller, BLUE scarf with trailing end, slower heavier gait. Kid: smallest, RED cap. Single-tone limbs, no ghost far-side layers.
narrative_beats: 0-41s (s01-07): giant locked door, every key fails, she forges her own key
41-82s (s08-14): golden key fails, handle snaps, despair, almost leaves, notices rusty hinge
82-123s (s15-21): stranger Oto helps oil hinge, she hammers pin with the broken handle, door opens the OTHER way
123-163s (s22-28): empty room, no prize, only tools; they repair, she props door open, kid peeks in
163-210s (s29-36): she welcomes kid, others build, room becomes workshop, keys become wind chime, CTA
thumbnail_concepts: Tiny stick figure holding a broken key beneath a giant door
Two stick figures lifting a heavy door hinge together
Open door illuminating an empty workshop with many new makers
title_alternatives: A Door for Tomorrow — The Key Was Never the Answer
She Tried Every Key. Then She Changed the Door.

growth_hypotheses: An instantly legible giant-door visual may improve first-five-second retention.
The key-versus-hinge reveal may create a satisfying rewatch.
An open-door communal payoff may support sharing; all hypotheses unvalidated.
creative_intent.sonic_signature: Recurring channel sound motif: key-ring jingle opens the film (s01) and the key wind chime closes it (s32, s36).
creative_intent.series_hook: s35 reveals a second locked giant door down the street; end-card question invites comments about viewers' own 'doors'.
